willing to do this.

Best,

Jonathan

Jonathan

is okay with you. Thanks!

Best,
Jonathan

messages.body:
Hello Grace,

I hope you are doing well. I am reaching out to you directly following the
introduction Doug made on my behalf. To briefly introduce myself, I am a
sophomore Economics and Business Student at the University of Texas,
Austin. I am interested in pursuing Tech Banking in NY, and would love to
speak with you to learn a little more about your experience at Barclays.

It would be great to connect either later this week or early next week.
Please let me know if you would be willing to chat. Attached is my resume.

Thanks,
Jonathan

messages.subject: Re: Potential favor
messages.body:
Hello Jay,

I hope you are doing well. I am reaching out to you directly following the
introduction Doug made on my behalf. To briefly introduce myself, I am a
sophomore Economics and Business Student at the University of Texas,
Austin. I am interested in pursuing Tech Banking in NY, and would love to
speak with you to learn a little more about your experience at Barclays.

It would be great to connect either later this week or early next week.
Please let me know if you would be willing to chat. Attached is my resume.

Best,
Jonathan

On Tue, Jan 30, 2024 at 2:54 PM <douglas.melsheimer@barclays.com> wrote:

> Jonathan, it was great speaking with you last week. As a next step, I’d
> like to introduce my colleagues Grace Steelman and Jay Klein (copied).
> Both are relatively new to Barclays and can help you navigate the analyst
> experience, either speaking with them directly, or to some of our other
> colleagues in the technology team.
>
>
>
> Will let you guys take it from here, but as I mentioned, happy to speak
> again any time as you move through the process and need some advice. Either
> way, you’ll be in good hands.
>
>
>
> Doug

messages.body:
Hi Jonathan –

Thank you for reaching out. I would be happy to hop on the phone. Please sending me your availability for later this week, and hopefully we can find a time!

Best,
Grace

From: Jonathan Nachman <jnachman17@gmail.com>
Sent: Tuesday, January 30, 2024 4:06 PM
To: Steelman, Grace : Investment Banking <grace.steelman@barclays.com>
Subject: Re: Potential favor

CAUTION: This email originated from outside our organisation - jnachman17@gmail.com<mailto:jnachman17@gmail.com> Do not click on links, open attachments, or respond unless you recognize the sender and can validate the content is safe.
Hello Grace,

I hope you are doing well. I am reaching out to you directly following the introduction Doug made on my behalf. To briefly introduce myself, I am a sophomore Economics and Business Student at the University of Texas, Austin. I am interested in pursuing Tech Banking in NY, and would love to speak with you to learn a little more about your experience at Barclays.

It would be great to connect either later this week or early next week. Please let me know if you would be willing to chat. Attached is my resume.

Thanks,
Jonathan

On Tue, Jan 30, 2024 at 2:54 PM <douglas.melsheimer@barclays.com<mailto:douglas.melsheimer@barclays.com>> wrote:
Jonathan, it was great speaking with you last week. As a next step, I’d like to introduce my colleagues Grace Steelman and Jay Klein (copied). Both are relatively new to Barclays and can help you navigate the analyst experience, either speaking with them directly, or to some of our other colleagues in the technology team.

Will let you guys take it from here, but as I mentioned, happy to speak again any time as you move through the process and need some advice. Either way, you’ll be in good hands.

Doug

Grace – I appreciate your quick response. Here are some times (ET) that
work for me this week and early next week.

Wednesday (1/31): 12:30 pm - 2:30 pm & 4 pm onwards
Thursday (2/1): 11:30 am - 2:30 pm & 6 pm onwards
Friday (2/2): 3:30 pm onwards
Monday (1/5): 12:30 pm onwards
Tuesday (1/6): 11:30 am - 2:30 pm & 6 pm onwards

Please let me know if any of these times are convenient for you. I look
forward to speaking soon.

Best,
Jonathan

messages.subject: Re: Potential favor
messages.body:
Hello Grace,

I wanted to thank you for spending the time with me today over the phone to
talk about your recruitment process and your experience at Barclays New
York. I am very appreciative of your willingness to offer insight as I am
still navigating this process and determining what I am looking for. To
that end, I looked on LinkedIn for the name of the Barclays MD who is a
Texas alum, but realized he is in the Houston office. However, I was able
to find an analyst in New York from UT Austin. His name is Jesse Chou. If
you can use your internal database and send over his email that would be
much appreciated. Thanks again!

Best,
Jonathan

Hi Jonathan –

Great speaking with you yesterday. His email is jesse.chou@barclays.com<mailto:jesse.chou@barclays.com>. It looks like he is not in the Investment Banking Division and works out of the Whippany, NJ office.

Best,
Grace

CAUTION: This email originated from outside our organisation - jnachman17@gmail.com<mailto:jnachman17@gmail.com> Do not click on links, open attachments, or respond unless you recognize the sender and can validate the content is safe.
Hello Grace,

I wanted to thank you for spending the time with me today over the phone to talk about your recruitment process and your experience at Barclays New York. I am very appreciative of your willingness to offer insight as I am still navigating this process and determining what I am looking for. To that end, I looked on LinkedIn for the name of the Barclays MD who is a Texas alum, but realized he is in the Houston office. However, I was able to find an analyst in New York from UT Austin. His name is Jesse Chou. If you can use your internal database and send over his email that would be much appreciated. Thanks again!

Best,
Jonathan

messages.subject: UT Austin Student & PGN Member Interested in Banking @ Goldman New York
messages.body:
Hello Sam,

I hope you are doing well. I am a Fall PC ‘22 PGN member studying Business and Economics, and I'm pursuing a career in Investment Banking. I'd love to talk to you to learn more about your experience at Goldman in New York. I am particularly interested in Banking in New York, so I would greatly appreciate the opportunity to speak with you.

If you have any free time in the next week, it would be great to set up a quick phone call with you. I am pretty open and can likely adjust my schedule to accommodate whatever works best for you. Please let me know if you would be willing to do this. Attached is my resume.

Best,
Jonathan

messages.body:
Hey Josh,

Thanks for spending the time to speak with me today about your recruiting
process and experience at FT Partners. You provided some very valuable
insight into the industry for me. If you could either connect me with or
forward along the contact info of the analyst at FT who interned in Houston
for a summer and then re-recruited that would be great. Additionally, I'll
definitely be applying to FT when applications open up down the road.
Thanks again!

Best,
Jonathan

messages.body:

Jonathan

Carson

Have a great weekend!

John Sellingsloh

Seeking advice on Banking @ Houlihan [Chadwick Alum & UT Austin Student)
messages.body:
Hello Kevin,

I hope you are doing well. My name is Jonathan Nachman, and I'm a
sophomore Economics and Business Student at The University of Texas,
Austin.

I was speaking with your daughter, Zoe, last night at a Chadwick dinner,
where I learned of our mutual interest in pursuing Investment Banking. She
had mentioned to me your role at Houlihan and expressed your willingness to
be a point of contact for me.

Coincidentally, I was on the phone today with Kate Borden, another Chadwick
alum and current analyst at Houlihan LA (CFR group). I am extremely
interested in your firm and would love to set up a quick phone call to gain
some more insight from you as a more senior banker. Please let me know if
you have any time to call next week.

Best,
Jonathan

--
*Jonathan Nachman *
University of Texas, Austin
Economics & Business
M: (310)-292-4712

messages.subject: [Josh Gumm Referral] UT Austin Student Interested in Banking @ FT
messages.body:
Hello Ethan,

I hope you are doing well. My name is Jonathan Nachman, and I'm an
Economics and Business student at the University of Texas, Austin. I had
the opportunity to speak to Josh Gumm on the phone yesterday regarding the
Summer Analyst Internship program at FT Partners, where he filled me in
briefly on your background. Given your unique experience spending a summer
as an Analyst in Houston to ultimately re-recruiting, I think you could
provide me with some very valuable insight coming from UT.

If you have any free time in the next week, I would love to set up a quick
phone call with you. I am pretty open and can likely adjust my schedule to
accommodate whatever works best for you. Please let me know if you would be
willing to do this. Attached is my resume.

Best,
Jonathan

*Jonathan Nachman *
University of Texas, Austin
Economics & Business

messages.body:

We would like to offer you a first round interview for the Morgan Stanley Houston Summer 2025 Analyst Internship. The team has enjoyed getting to know you and thinks you could be a great fit for this role.

-Matt

Hi Jonathan,

Hope you are well! We understand that you are interested in our 2025 New York Financial Restructuring Summer Analyst opportunities at Houlihan Lokey and would like to set up a 30-minute introductory call with one of our bankers over the next few weeks. Best,
Maura Vestal, Senior Campus Recruiter

messages.subject: Thank you for applying to Aeris Partners
Potential Goldman IB NY RX Group Recruiting Scam
messages.body:
Hello Goldman Representatives,

I hope you are doing well. I am emailing you to inform you of a potential scam I have been subject to regarding a Goldman employee posing as a member of the New York Restructuring Group offering 1st round virtual interviews. Last night, I received an ambiguous text from a NY number, claiming to be someone by the name of Jacob Goldwich. This individual reached out via iMessage and claimed to be with Goldman, asking me to call him when I have a moment. I immediately looked up his name on LinkedIn and there was no profile matching his name, which I immediately deemed suspicious. Furthermore, it is very atypical for bankers to reach out over text, especially given your office hasn't opened applications, and I have not had any coffee chats with Goldman. I, however, called this individual and he claimed another NY bank I had been recruiting with shared my information and put in a recommendation behind my name. He said due to privacy contracts, he could not disclose which bank shared my information. Nonetheless, he said his office would like to offer me a virtual 1st round this upcoming Monday. He claimed HR would email me this morning to confirm a time for this interview, to which no email from HR was received. I am fairly confident this was a recruiting scam, yet I do not understand how this individual benefits from the scam as he did not ask me to hand over any personal information. However, he did know a fair bit about me, addressing me by my nickname which I have not included on any recruiting applications, as well as some of my basic background information. I found your webpage online titled "Recruiting Scams Alert" and it described this situation. Therefore, I am emailing this address to simply let you know of this occurrence. Hopefully, this email provided some valuable information to your office. Please let me know if you have any questions.

All the best,
Jonathan
